prompt:
You are a grounded brand-outreach assistant for our team. Use only the evidence passages below.
Never use outside knowledge. Return valid JSON only.

Separate three things:
1. OBSERVED FACTS - things a passage actually states about this company. Each fact is a claim with an id (C1, C2, ...),
   the passage id(s) that support it, and an exact quote copied word-for-word from that passage.
2. UNKNOWNS - things the evidence does not tell us (put them in "unknowns"). A channel, program or audience that does
   not appear in these passages is UNKNOWN. It is never a weakness, never a "gap", and never a reason for outreach.
3. PROPOSALS - collaboration ideas from our team. Proposals are not facts, but each must build on a positively supported
   fact (an existing campaign, partnership, product, community, value or theme) and cite that premise.

Rules:
- Put a claim marker like {C1} (curly braces) right after every factual statement in every field, including the
  email and Instagram idea. Do not write citation numbers yourself; markers are converted to citations later.
- A claim's "quote" must be copied character-for-character from the cited passage: 5 to 25 consecutive words, no
  paraphrasing, no joining of separate sentences. If you cannot find such a quote, drop the claim and every sentence
  that depends on it.
- Audience and strategy sentences are factual: each needs a marker. If no passage states the audience, write
  INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of guessing.
- Pitch lines (email subject, hook, concept) should describe the proposed post ("A carousel featuring ...",
  "Collaborate on ..."). Any statement in them about what the company already does needs a marker.
- Respect passage types. "proposed_or_mock_work" and "author_recommendation" passages describe ideas, not things the
  company did: never state them as company activity. "provider_reported_result" passages are claims by a vendor or
  agency: attribute them ("X reports that ..."). "creator_or_influencer_audience_data" describes creators' followers,
  not the company's customers. "vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics" passages are a tool vendor's estimates
  (e.g. inferred age ranges): attribute them and never present them as the company's own data.
  "forward_looking_statement" passages describe plans or intentions, not completed activity.
- Mind time: if a passage describes past activity, do not present it as current.
- "marketing_gaps" may only contain a weakness that a passage positively states. Usually it is [].
- Never promise results. Describe benefits as goals or possibilities ("could", "aims to"), not guaranteed outcomes.
- Decision: write "draft" when at least one concrete, evidence-supported collaboration opportunity exists. Otherwise write
  "abstain", give an abstain_reason, set pitch fields to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and leave collaboration_opportunities empty.
- The email is from our team to the company, proposing one collaborative Instagram post. The pitch, the post idea and
  every collaboration opportunity are for Instagram only (no TikTok, YouTube, podcasts or other channels).
- When a sentence uses a vendor, agency or analytics passage, name that source in the sentence itself
  ("According to AdLibrary, ...", "Attentive reports that ...").
- Each "unknowns" item names one specific thing the passages do not tell us (e.g. "Whether X runs a creator program").
  Never write placeholder text such as "what the evidence does not show".

Required JSON:
{
  "decision": "draft" or "abstain",
  "abstain_reason": "string or empty",
  "claims": [{"id": "C1", "kind": "fact | provider_reported | premise", "statement": "string",
              "passage_ids": ["P1"], "quote": "exact words from the passage"}],
  "brand_summary": "Full sentences, each followed by its marker, e.g. "X makes ... {C1}." Never only markers. Or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "likely_target_audience": "A full sentence followed by its marker, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "current_marketing_strategy": ["text with markers"],
  "unknowns": ["one specific open question, e.g. Whether the company works with creators"],
  "marketing_gaps": [],
  "collaboration_opportunities": ["proposal that builds on a cited fact {C2}"],
  "instagram_post_idea": {"hook": "string", "concept": "string", "why_it_fits": "string"},
  "email_subject": "string",
  "email_body": "string"
}

Company: Misfits Market (company_id misfits-market; category: online value grocery)
Official domains: misfitsmarket.com
Recipient: the marketing team
Packet status: ok

Evidence passages:
[P1] source: https://www.misfitsmarket.com/about-us | document: official_domain | type: historical_activity | flags: forward_looking_statement | dates in text: 2018 | published: unknown
"Farmer Spotlight: Lakeside Organic Gardens We’ve been proud to offer Lakeside’s standout California-grown organic veggies since 2018, but our partnership goes even deeper. When they told us trimmed broccoli florets were going to waste during routine fieldwork, we collaborated to package them up as Sweet Broccoli Tops. That kind of teamwork is an easy (and delicious way!) to save food waste, while offering customers big savings."

[P2] source: https://www.misfitsmarket.com/about-us | document: official_domain | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"And with a degree in agriculture, she knows just how important supporting farmers and fighting food waste is. ## Fighting food waste adds up We ran the numbers—when we save food from waste, we also save all the resources that went into producing it. In the last year alone we saved..."

[P3] source: https://shahidshahmiri.com/misfits-market/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Referral and word-of-mouth marketing are also central to Misfits Market’s growth. The brand encourages existing customers to invite friends and family by offering credits or discounts, effectively turning satisfied users into brand advocates. Because the product experience is closely tied to a social mission, referrals feel more natural and less transactional. In addition, Misfits Market leverages influencer and creator partnerships to reach niche audiences. Collaborations with sustainability advocates, food creators, and lifestyle influencers help the brand build credibility while showcasing real-life use cases."

[P4] source: https://shahidshahmiri.com/misfits-market/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"This makes the mission feel accessible to a broader audience, not just environmentally conscious consumers. Visually and verbally, Misfits Market reinforces transparency. Product descriptions, sourcing explanations, and educational content help reduce skepticism around “imperfect” food. This trust-building approach is critical in online grocery, where customers cannot physically inspect products before purchase. From a marketing strategy perspective, this consistent messaging ensures that every touchpoint, website copy, emails, social media and advertisements, reinforces the same core narrative."

[P5] source: https://shahidshahmiri.com/misfits-market/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Social Media & Community Building Social media plays a vital role in how Misfits Market builds brand affinity and community rather than just driving direct sales. The brand focuses on platforms where visual storytelling and short-form content perform well, using them to highlight real products, customer experiences, and sustainability impact. User-generated content is a key part of this strategy. By featuring customers, unboxing moments, recipes, and before-and-after grocery hauls, Misfits Market turns everyday usage into social proof. This helps potential customers see the product in a real-world context, reducing skepticism and increasing trust."

[P6] source: https://www.misfitsmarket.com/about-us | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: 2018 | published: unknown
"28.5 million pounds of total food from lesser outcomes For a total of 238 million pounds since 2018! ## We put community first A more sustainable food system means access to nutritious food for everyone. But right now, 1 in 7 people face hunger*—while a third of all U.S. food goes to waste**. That’s why we partner with 60+ organizations nationwide, including Feeding America, to fight hunger and improve food access everywhere we operate. Learn more here."

generator.quote_repair: claims.repair_quotes (min similarity 0.9; numbers/negations unchanged); see attempts[].quote_repairs
generator.note: repair rounds show the teacher only its own draft and the failed check messages
